section: Centre-State legislative relations - Articles 245-255, doctrine of repugnancy, parliamentary legislation on state list
subsections: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition
Article 249 resolution - Rajya Sabha majority, duration, extension
Conflict between lists - Article 246, order of precedence

accepted.s: Under which constitutional provision may Parliament legislate on a matter in the State List when it is necessary in the national interest?
o: Article 250
Article 249
Article 252
Article 248
accepted.x: Article 249 enables Parliament to legislate on State List matters in the national interest, subject to a resolution of the Rajya Sabha supported by the prescribed majority.
accepted.tq: Use the article-condition pair to distinguish the special legislative powers.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. National interest — Article 249
2. National Emergency — Article 250
3. Request of two or more States — Article 252
4. International agreements — Article 253
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Articles 249, 250, 252 and 253 respectively concern national interest, Emergency, State resolutions and international agreements.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure article-condition pairs and eliminate codes containing a wrong pairing.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Parliament may legislate on a State List subject under Article 250 when:
o: the President receives an international treaty
a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation
the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution in the national interest
two or more State Legislatures request it
accepted.x: Article 250 operates while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation and permits Parliament to make laws on State List matters.
accepted.tq: Identify the triggering condition rather than recalling the article number alone.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Article 252, consider the following statements:
1. The legislatures of two or more States must pass resolutions requesting parliamentary legislation.
2. Any other State may adopt the resulting law later by passing a resolution of its legislature.
3. The requesting State Legislatures may independently repeal the law enacted by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: only Parliament can amend or repeal a law enacted under Article 252.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that assigns legislative power to the wrong authority.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an example of legislation enacted under Article 252?
o: Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Prize Competition Act, 1955
accepted.x: The Prize Competition Act, 1955, Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 and Water Act, 1974 are examples associated with Article 252. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is not included in the listed examples.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the specified group of Article 252 examples.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following Acts is associated with parliamentary legislation under Article 252?
1. Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976
2. Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994
3. Prize Competition Act, 1955
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three Acts are listed as examples of laws enacted by Parliament under Article 252 following resolutions by two or more State Legislatures.
accepted.tq: Test the complete list by checking whether each named example belongs to the same constitutional route.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 356, legislation for a State during President’s Rule may be made by:
o: Parliament, or the President under delegated authority
the Governor alone without constitutional authority
the State Legislature alone
the Inter-State Council
accepted.x: During President’s Rule, Parliament may legislate for the State; the President may also exercise this legislative function when Parliament delegates it.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the competent authority.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A law made for a State during President’s Rule continues after the Proclamation ends until:
o: the State Legislature alters, repeals or re-enacts it
the Supreme Court declares it permanent
the Governor issues an ordinance replacing it
the Parliament automatically repeals it
accepted.x: Such a law does not automatically lapse when President’s Rule ends. It continues until the State Legislature alters, repeals or re-enacts it.
accepted.tq: Test the post-emergency effect instead of confusing continuation with automatic repeal.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Article empowers Parliament to make laws for the whole or any part of India to implement treaties, agreements and conventions?
o: Article 252
Article 253
Article 254
Article 251
accepted.x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate for the whole or any part of India for implementing treaties, agreements and conventions.
accepted.tq: Match the international-law purpose with its specific constitutional provision.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of a Parliamentary law made under Article 249 or Article 250 when it conflicts with a State law?
o: The Governor decides which law will prevail.
The Parliamentary law prevails over the State law.
The State law prevails because State subjects remain exclusively State matters.
Both laws become void to the extent of conflict.
accepted.x: Article 251 provides that a Parliamentary law made under Article 249 or 250 prevails over an inconsistent State law.
accepted.tq: Use the conflict rule to identify the superior law and reject the wrong authority.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The resolution authorising Parliament to legislate on a State List matter in the national interest is passed by:
o: the Rajya Sabha by two-thirds of members present and voting
the Rajya Sabha by a majority of the total membership
the Lok Sabha by a simple majority
both Houses by a special majority
accepted.x: Article 249 requires a resolution of the Rajya Sabha supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting. The Lok Sabha does not participate in passing this resolution.
accepted.tq: Separate the required House from the exact form of majority.
accepted.sec: Article 249 resolution - Rajya Sabha majority, duration, extension  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a resolution under Article 249:
1. It remains in force for a period not exceeding one year.
2. It may be renewed any number of times.
3. Each renewal may extend it for a period exceeding one year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: every renewal can extend the resolution only for one year at a time.
accepted.tq: Watch the limiting phrase ‘one year at a time’ in a duration question.
accepted.sec: Article 249 resolution - Rajya Sabha majority, duration, extension  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A resolution of the Rajya Sabha under Article 249 can be renewed:
o: any number of times, one year at a time
indefinitely without a fixed renewal period
only twice for one year each
only once for six months
accepted.x: The resolution may be renewed any number of times, but each renewal is limited to one year.
accepted.tq: Distinguish unlimited renewals from an unlimited duration for each renewal.
accepted.sec: Article 249 resolution - Rajya Sabha majority, duration, extension  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A law made by Parliament under Article 249 ceases to have effect:
o: six months before the resolution lapses
only when the State Legislature passes a contrary law
immediately when the Rajya Sabha resolution lapses
six months after the resolution lapses
accepted.x: A law enacted under Article 249 continues for six months after the resolution authorising it lapses, after which it ceases to operate.
accepted.tq: Focus on the delayed legal effect rather than the date on which the enabling resolution ends.
accepted.sec: Article 249 resolution - Rajya Sabha majority, duration, extension  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding State legislative power during the operation of Article 249 is correct?
o: The State Legislature may legislate only after obtaining the consent of the Rajya Sabha.
The State Legislature’s power is suspended, but the Governor may legislate.
The State Legislature may still legislate, but the Parliamentary law prevails in case of conflict.
The State Legislature is dissolved for the entire duration of the resolution.
accepted.x: An Article 249 resolution does not suspend the State Legislature’s power. However, the Parliamentary law prevails if it conflicts with a State law.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme claim that a special Union power automatically removes State legislative power.
accepted.sec: Article 249 resolution - Rajya Sabha majority, duration, extension  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During a Proclamation of Emergency, which one of the following is constitutionally correct?
o: The Prime Minister alone may legislate on State List matters.
Only the President may enact ordinary laws on State List matters.
Parliament may legislate on State List matters for the whole or any part of India.
The State Legislature loses all legislative powers permanently.
accepted.x: Article 250 permits Parliament to legislate on State List matters for the whole or any part of India while the Emergency is in operation.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional law-making body instead of a minister or individual executive authority.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Laws made by Parliament under Article 250 become inoperative:
o: three months after the Emergency ends
six months after the Emergency ends
one year after the Emergency ends
immediately on the withdrawal of the Emergency
accepted.x: A law made under Article 250 becomes inoperative six months after the Proclamation of Emergency ceases to operate.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the six-month post-Emergency period from the duration of the Emergency itself.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following provisions in chronological order of their Article numbers:
A. Legislation in national interest
B. Legislation during National Emergency
C. Legislation on request of two or more States
D. Legislation for implementing international agreements
o: A, B, C, D
B, A, C, D
A, C, B, D
D, C, B, A
accepted.x: The provisions correspond respectively to Articles 249, 250, 252 and 253. Therefore, the correct order is A, B, C, D.
accepted.tq: Convert each description into its article number and then arrange the numbers.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 246, the power of Parliament to make laws is exclusive in respect of matters contained in:
o: List I of the Seventh Schedule
all three Lists without limitation
List II of the Seventh Schedule
List III of the Seventh Schedule
accepted.x: Article 246(1) gives Parliament exclusive power over matters in the Union List, or List I, subject to the constitutional provisions.
accepted.tq: Match each clause of Article 246 with the corresponding legislative list.
accepted.sec: Conflict between lists - Article 246, order of precedence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects Article 246?
1. Parliament has exclusive power over List I.
2. Parliament and State Legislatures can both legislate over List III.
3. State Legislatures have power over List II, subject to Parliament’s powers under Article 246(1) and 246(2).
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe Articles 246(1), 246(2) and 246(3), respectively.
accepted.tq: Check each sub-clause separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Conflict between lists - Article 246, order of precedence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A law made by a State Legislature under the State List conflicts with a valid law made by Parliament under the Concurrent List. Which law ordinarily prevails?
o: The Parliamentary law, because the Concurrent List has precedence over the State List
The later law, irrespective of the legislative body
The law approved by the Governor
The State law, because the subject is administered by the State
accepted.x: The Concurrent List has precedence over the State List. Therefore, a valid Parliamentary law on a Concurrent List matter ordinarily prevails over an inconsistent State law.
accepted.tq: Apply the order of precedence to a concrete conflict rather than relying on administrative control.
accepted.sec: Conflict between lists - Article 246, order of precedence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 246(4), Parliament may make laws on any matter for:
o: areas not included in a State, such as Union Territories
foreign territories alone
only the States included in List II
only areas declared by the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Article 246(4) enables Parliament to legislate on any matter for any part of the territory of India not included in a State, including Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Use the territorial exception in Article 246(4) to identify the correct scope.
accepted.sec: Conflict between lists - Article 246, order of precedence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 246(4):
1. Parliament may legislate for Union Territories on matters in all three Lists.
2. The legislative power of Parliament for Union Territories is confined to the Union List.
3. The provision applies to areas not included in a State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Parliament’s power for Union Territories extends to all three Lists, not merely the Union List.
accepted.tq: Spot the restrictive word ‘confined’ and compare it with the wider territorial power.
accepted.sec: Conflict between lists - Article 246, order of precedence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to Article 246A, which one of the following is correct regarding Goods and Services Tax legislation?
o: Parliament and State Legislatures have no power over GST without a Rajya Sabha resolution.
Only Parliament can make GST laws, including laws on intra-State supply.
Only State Legislatures can make GST laws.
Both Parliament and State Legislatures can make GST laws, but Parliament has exclusive power over inter-State supply.
accepted.x: Article 246A gives both Parliament and State Legislatures power to make GST laws. Parliament has exclusive power regarding GST on inter-State supplies, including IGST matters.
accepted.tq: Separate the shared GST power from Parliament’s exclusive inter-State competence.
accepted.sec: Conflict between lists - Article 246, order of precedence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Article 246A was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
o: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act
The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act
accepted.x: Article 246A was introduced by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, which established the constitutional framework for GST.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive constitutional article with the amendment that introduced it.
accepted.sec: Conflict between lists - Article 246, order of precedence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the five constitutional situations in which Parliament may legislate on State List matters?
o: Article 252 operates when one State Legislature alone requests parliamentary legislation.
Article 356 operates during President’s Rule in a State.
Article 249 deals with national interest.
Article 250 operates during a Proclamation of Emergency.
accepted.x: Article 252 requires resolutions from the legislatures of two or more States, not one State Legislature alone. Articles 249, 250 and 356 are correctly described.
accepted.tq: Test the minimum numerical condition and reject the deceptively shortened requirement.
accepted.sec: Parliament legislating on State List → article and condition  [APPSC]
